entries.title: World Soil Day Competition — entries close 4 December
entries.description:
A soil-health competition for primary producers, Landcare or similar groups, and First Nations groups caring for agricultural or grazing land in northern NSW or southern Queensland. Share a practice that improves soil health or a soil problem you want to address, and explain its relevance to drought and climatic extremes.

Entries close Friday 4 December 2026 at 11:59pm AEST (Queensland time). In NSW daylight-saving time, that is 12:59am on Saturday 5 December. This listing marks an entry deadline, not an in-person gathering.

Entry is free. Three winners receive soil assessment packages valued at $5,000 each, including a site visit, soil testing and a report; these are services rather than cash prizes.

Enter by email to sqnnswhub@unisq.edu.au or follow the organiser’s social-media entry instructions. Check the full eligibility and competition terms before submitting.

entries.title: North Coast Beef Producers Field Day 2026
entries.description:
Join North Coast Local Land Services for a field day exploring crossbreeding, herd productivity, meat quality, profitability and supply-chain opportunities for North Coast beef producers.

When: Thursday 3 December 2026, arrive at 8:30am for a 9am start; finishes at 2pm NSW time.
Where: Grafton Primary Industries Institute, Experiment Farm Road, Trenayr NSW 2460.

Registration is free. Morning tea and lunch are provided; the organiser asks people with dietary requirements to bring their own food. Register through the organiser’s Humanitix page.

entries.title: Rehydrate Australia — film, supper and discussion at Pearces Creek Hall
entries.description:
Watch Rehydrate Australia, a documentary about farmers restoring landscapes through Natural Sequence Farming, followed by a discussion with Stuart Andrews of Tarwyn Park Training and Josh Wellman of Banyula Farm. Hosted by Pearces Creek Talks with Pearces Creek Hall.

When: Saturday 14 November 2026. Doors and supper from 6:30pm NSW time; the event header lists a 9pm finish.
Where: Pearces Creek Hall, 40 Pearces Creek Hall Road, Pearces Creek NSW 2477.

Tickets are advertised at $5 for adults, with children aged 16 and under free. A supper plate is included; drinks are BYO. Book through Humanitix.

For a practical follow-up, the Natural Sequence Farming Field Day at Banyula Farm runs the next day, Sunday 15 November.

entries.title: Darren Doherty — farm planning for agroforestry recordings
entries.description:
Watch the two-part farm-planning workshop hosted by Byron Shire Council and the Byron Farmers Network at Federal Hall earlier in 2026. Darren Doherty explores agroforestry design and practical planning, including LiDAR and GIS mapping tools.

These are recordings available to watch anytime, not a new scheduled workshop.

Part 1 — Farm Planning for Agroforestry with Darren Doherty and the Byron Farmers Network:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=86L9xPeMiM8

Part 2 — Farm planning and mapping for agroforestry integration: a practical demo:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e1PPpjAKduQ

Both videos are published on Byron Shire Council’s YouTube channel.
